Loads a picture file as a texture and returns its handle, or 0 if the file cannot be read. PNG, JPG, BMP, TGA (by the extension `.tga`), GIF, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, DDS and some other formats are supported (see [Image formats](Image-Formats)), but not TIFF or JPEG 2000. Loading the same file twice gives two separate textures.

DDS files that are block compressed (DXT1 to DXT5, BC4 and BC7) are sent to the graphics card as they are when it supports the format, which is nearly every desktop card. They then use a quarter to an eighth of the video memory of a PNG of the same size. A texture is turned into an ordinary 32 bit one the first time it is drawn to, for example with SetBuffer and TextureBuffer, which uses the full amount of memory from then on. A compressed file is decoded when it is loaded instead if the card cannot use its format, if flag 4 (masked) is given, if flag 2 is given and the file has no see-through pixels (it then gets its alpha from how bright it is), or if it is BC5, whose third channel is rebuilt. Without flag 2 the texture is opaque, as for every other file.

These formats are read: the block compressed DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5 (BC1, BC2 and BC3), ATI1 and ATI2 (BC4 and BC5) and BC7, including the BC1 to BC7 formats of files with a `DX10` header and their sRGB variants, the common uncompressed `DX10` formats (RGBA8, BGRA8, BGRX8, 5:6:5, 5:5:5:1, 4:4:4:4, R8, RG8 and A8), and uncompressed RGB, RGBA, luminance and alpha-only pictures with 8, 16, 24 or 32 bits and any bit masks. BC4 pictures are shown as grey, and BC5 pictures as a normal map. DXT1 has see-through pixels if a block uses a see-through color. BC6H (HDR) and files with 16 bit float or 32 bit float channels are not read. Cube maps, volume textures and texture arrays give their first face, slice or layer.

Mip maps (flag 8, which [TextureFilter](TextureFilter) adds to every texture at the start) make distant surfaces use smaller, blurrier copies of the texture. Without the flag only the biggest picture of the file is used. With it, the mip maps that are stored in a block compressed DDS file are used as they are and stay compressed, so a texture with a full chain needs a third more video memory than without. A file that has no stored mip maps, or only some, gets the missing ones made when it is loaded: each is the average of 2 by 2 texels of the one above it, down to a single texel. A compressed file without stored mip maps is decoded for this, and then uses the full amount of memory, as do the ones that are decoded for the reasons above. Stored mip maps of uncompressed DDS files are not read, the whole chain is made from the biggest picture. Drawing on a texture with [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer) makes the mip maps again from the picture as it is then, before the texture is next drawn in a scene.

How transparency is taken from the file depends on the flags. Without flag 2 the picture is opaque even if the file has an alpha channel. With flag 2 an existing alpha channel is used, and a picture without one gets its alpha from how bright each texel is. Flag 4 makes every pure black texel transparent and everything else opaque.

Textures that [TextureFilter](TextureFilter) matches by file name get extra flags added.

```blitzbasic
;media still textures/loadtexture.png
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
CameraClsColor camera, 70, 100, 160
light = CreateLight()
RotateEntity light, 40, 30, 0

; Make a file with a white disc on black, then load it back as a masked texture.
src = CreateTexture(64, 64)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(src)
ClsColor 0, 0, 0
Cls
Color 255, 200, 40
Oval 4, 4, 56, 56, 1
SaveBuffer TextureBuffer(src), "wiki_disc.bmp"
SetBuffer BackBuffer()

solid = LoadTexture("wiki_disc.bmp", 1)
masked = LoadTexture("wiki_disc.bmp", 1 + 4)
a = CreateCube() : PositionEntity a, -1.3, 0, 5 : EntityTexture a, solid
b = CreateCube() : PositionEntity b, 1.3, 0, 5 : EntityTexture b, masked
TurnEntity a, 20, 30, 0
TurnEntity b, 20, 30, 0
RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```

![LoadTexture](media/textures/loadtexture.png)
@param file   Picture file to load.
@param flags  Sum of the texture flags, see CreateTexture. Defaults to 1.
@returns A texture handle, or 0 if the file could not be loaded.
@gap TIFF and JPEG 2000 files do not load, which the original read. WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL and DDS load instead, see [Image formats](Image-Formats).
@gap Video memory, high color and point sampling flags are stored but have no effect, see CreateTexture. A sphere map (64) uses the whole picture. A cube map (128) needs a picture of six faces next to each other, in the order of SetCubeFace, and gives 0 if its width cannot be divided by 6.
